newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ANALYSTS COMMENTS ON HEINEKEN '96 RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: ANALYSTS COMMENTS ON HEINEKEN '96 RESULTS.

text.p: Dutch brewer Heineken NV on Friday reported 1996 net profits of 655 million guilders against 664 million in 1995. Analysts had expected Europe's largest brewer to post a net of between 630 and 660 million guilders.
The company said it expected to see profit growth in 1997, but could not yet say how much.
Below is a collection of analysts' comments on the results:
DARRELL DUTHIE AT MEEPIERSON:
"The figures are somewhat at the upper range of expectations, the composition looks fine. As expected, acquisitions added to the increase in turnover.
"The outlook is interesting. Heineken is cautious and it looks as if it is trying to temper expectations somewhat.
"What it says about the shift towards drinking at home isn't new. We've been seeing that in England for a while and England often is ahead of the other markets.
"But they say the company will only benefit to a small extent from the dollar's appreciation in 1997 as they have hedged cash flows for some time.
"I think that will disappoint some, as they had expected Heineken to benefit much more from the dollar's rise."
HANS PLUIJGERS AT KEMPEN & CO:

"The result was at the upper range of expectations. Underlying operational results have improved, and the loss of volume in Europe has had only a limited impact. Apparently, exports have partly compensated for the fixed costs.
"As expected, margins were pressured by the decrease in volume and the bigger marketing efforts. They will remain so in Europe due to the increased marketing costs.
"I think their comments on 1997 are not bad. Usually, they don't give a forecast for the year at such an early stage, but stick to long-term prospects."
TON MULLER AT NIB SECURITIES:
"The figures were in line with the expectations.
"The bad weather in Europe cost almost one million hectolitres in consumption, resulting in some 50 million guilders less in the net profit.
"I expect 1997 profits to be some ten percent above last year. The comparative figure is relatively low, and the company in itself should be able to attain nice profit growth.
"European beer markets are stagnating, but in one or two years, Heineken will benefit from economies of scale due to its French acquisitions.
"In Asia, beer consumption continues to surge and I think a six to seven percent growth in the American import beer segment can be counted on over the next five years or so.
"The company has an enormous amount of liquidity which it can use for investments or further acquisitions to enhance growth.
"We still rate the stock an underperformer, but that's because of the high valuation."
CORNE ZANDBERGEN, GENERALE BANK:
"It was more or less in line with our expectations and there were no real surprises. We were, however, a little surprised by the high increase in personnel costs.
"In the first half, they went up by about 20 percent and in the second half by 31 percent, although it seems to be linked to restructuring as well as acquisitions.
"Acquisitions themselves appear to have depressed margins, but we don't expect to change our recommendations."
CEES HAASNOOT AT EFFECTENBANK STROEVE:

"The results were fine, but the share surging 13 guilders in early trade was an overreaction. I think it was also in relief after Grolsch' figures disappointed on Wednesday. People tend to compare Heineken with Grolsch, which makes no sense.

"Everybody can brew beer, what counts is marketing and distribution. Heineken is the world's most international brewer when looked at geographical spread. It's always one step ahead when moving into growth markets.
"Next to Europe as a saturated cash-cow, Heineken is active in Asia, Latin America, the U.S...which will all contribute to strong long-term growth.
"You have to differentiate between incidental and structural factors as well. A bad summer does not say anything about the company's fundamentals."
GERARD RIJK, ING BARINGS
"The results were broadly in line with expectations, but the profit forecast was very healthy for this time of year.
"The confidence of the company has increased in the past six months. Exports continue to grow and exchange rates are very much more positive.
"(The firm dollar) will have a strong impact for later in 1997 and in 1998 because of the delayed effect of the hedging. With its acquisitions, there are enormous cost savings possible.
"There are many positive factors. We had Heineken as a buy. That will stay and it should now start to outperform." -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
